cards.title: B-366: Falcon 2 OBJ and in-game barrel stretch
cards.description: Mike reported that Falcon 2 loads with the end of the barrel stretched/skewed and the extracted OBJ has the same bad shape, then asked to check all weapons for a model extraction process issue. He later confirmed the in-game stretch persisted with the tip staying fixed while the model moved.
cards.notes:
Code/build/smoke verified 2026-05-22; pending Mike's visual retest of Falcon 2 in-game and its extracted OBJ before closure. Extracted OBJ root cause was .pdmesh OBJ export ignoring G_MTX/G_POPMTX modelview commands and the SPSEGMENT_MODEL_MTX table used by weapon display lists, so local unposed weapon parts could be written into OBJ data and then embedded into .pdweapon archives. The exporter now builds default model matrices from model position nodes, applies the matrix stack while emitting OBJ vertices, writes model_obj_mtx_v8/export_version.txt metadata, and bumps .pdmesh plus .pdweapon cache markers through embedded.v9 / pdweapon_embedded_v9 so stale standalone and nested held meshes rebuild. The final Falcon source-mesh pass culls the detached transformed effect group only for FILE_GFALCON2 / FILE_GFALCON2LOD, removing the skewed OBJ barrel-end group without applying that cull globally. Remaining in-game root cause matched Mike's tip-fixed-while-model-moved clue: the Falcon laser beam far endpoint was projected from the crosshair while the near endpoint followed the muzzle/root. bgunUpdateLasersight now derives both near and far endpoints from the muzzle matrix/local forward vector before projection, while the steady-state gate keeps stale equip/busy beams hidden. Verification: focused mesh extractor test passed with 80 assertions / 1 case; focused .pdweapon test passed with 65 assertions / 1 case; focused [bondgun][laser][static] passed with 25 assertions / 4 cases; isolated falconbeam5 all-target build passed; boot_smoke passed 14/14 and wrote 303 .pdmesh plus 86 .pdweapon archives; Falcon OBJ reports 422 triangles, 4 display lists, 8 matrix commands, 8 model-matrix references, and FILE_GFALCON2; the previous severe-Y detached group is absent; mixed severe-Y detached scan across generated weapon meshes found 0. Broad c3812 static selector still has one unrelated pre-existing scenario visual-export literal assertion.

cards.title: Input: press/hold canonical actions
cards.description: Press/Hold canonical action handling in actionmap. Hold/tap first-class with actionHeldForMs, actionWasTap, actionConsumeHold, actionHoldProgress.
cards.notes: Closed 2026-05-21 after verification. Completed core: press/tap and hold share the same physical input state; actionWasTap consumes the short-release path by elapsed release time below threshold; actionHeldForMs gates the long-held path at or above threshold; actionConsumeHold prevents the later release from also firing tap; actionHoldProgress pins full briefly after consumption then returns to 0. Verified concrete consumers: ACTION_USE tap=reload / hold=interact+consume, ACTION_WEAPON_NEXT tap=cycle / hold=radial+consume, ACTION_CROUCH tap/hold stance state machine. Natural-stop cases are not a new actionmap primitive: interaction one-shot consumption is covered by ACTION_USE, and future ammo-empty/full-charge/beam/overheat/cooldown behavior belongs to c3814-s15 held-weapon runtime adapter consumer work.

cards.title: Rule 10 (skip-empty-bindings) lifted into universal grammar
cards.description: New Rule 10 in menu-input-interaction-grammar.md: focusable elements with no defined directional binding for an axis are SKIPPED during focus traversal in that axis -- focus does not stop on dead nodes. Generalises CC1 (section headers / dividers non-focusable) into a per-direction membership predicate. Three implementation strategies documented (mark non-focusable, per-direction NoNav, bindings-manifest gate). Source: Mike's directive 2026-05-03 'The things where I didn't put input should be skipped when navigating'. Codified as a v2 universal rule alongside the existing Rule 1 column-traversal semantic.

cards.title: B-356: Combat Sim post-match screen visible and interactive
cards.description: Mike reported that ending a Combat Simulator match appeared to route toward the post-match screen, but the post-match screen never appeared and the game had to be force-closed. Follow-up: the post-match window became visible but X did not close it and Quit/Disconnect buttons looked inert. Root causes: the MP game-over root could be hidden by the suppressed legacy NTSC Save Player dialog, then the visible endscreen opened confirm popups from the action-bar child scope while rendering them from the parent endscreen scope.
cards.notes:
Fixed 2026-05-21 in the same menu/input sweep. mpPushEndscreenDialog now marks OPTION_ASKEDSAVEPLAYER but does not push g_MpEndscreenSavePlayerMenuDialog on PC, so the MP game-over root remains visible and the ImGui endscreen exit path owns config saving. Second pass: MP and solo endscreen confirm popups now open from the parent endscreen scope after the action-bar child closes, and the custom title X accepts root/child focus so it still works after focus lands in the content/action children. Static coverage added to tests/test_menu_graph.cpp.

cards.title: Input: custom/accessibility controller class + glyph/social foundation
cards.description: Controller remains a first-class citizen, but custom devices need a privacy-safe path that does not pretend every non-MKB device is an Xbox-style gamepad. Add foundational support for SDL raw joystick devices such as HOTAS/HOSAS, homemade HID controllers, adaptive/accessibility devices, and button boxes through the existing action map/rebind pipeline. Surface only coarse input class metadata in glyphs and Social presence.
cards.notes:
Implemented and build-verified 2026-05-21 as the foundation slice. Raw non-SDL_GameController joysticks are opened alongside standard controllers, bind capture accepts raw buttons and axes 0-5, actionmap dispatch routes raw buttons/axes through existing JOY virtual keys, glyphs show BtnN/AxisN labels for custom-class devices, and Social presence v3 carries a privacy-safe input class. This intentionally does not expose device GUID/vendor/name over presence. c3819 adds the first per-device profile assignment layer; remaining deeper work is custom texture glyph packs, richer calibration/deadzone UI, automatic per-device profile activation policy, and more than six-axis semantic binding.

cards.title: B-323 post-boot AV in challengesInit (Pass C side-effect, N64-vs-PC stride)
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-03 (competent-saha-a202bb). Mike's playtest of dev 1363ee75 AVs at boot inside challengesInit() -- bcopy/memcpy+146 from a dmaExecWithAutoAlign over-read in src/game/challenge.c::challengeLoadConfig. Root cause: PC sizeof(struct mpconfig) = 4596 and sizeof(struct mpstrings) = 680 used as both stride and read length, but on-disk segment is laid out with N64 sizes (mpstrings 320 bytes/entry); MAX_BOTS grew 8 -> 32. Pre-Pass-C the over-read landed in adjacent ROM bytes inside the contiguous 32 MB g_RomFile -- harmless. Post-Pass-C (S607, dev b15cc701) each segment is its own heap allocation; over-read AVs. g_MpChallenges[0].confignum=14 makes the very first call attempt a 4596-byte read at offset 14*4596=64344, ~60 KB past the 4576-byte segment. Fix: (1) Remove mpconfigs dmaExec entirely (data was always overwritten by mpconfig->config = g_MpConfigs[confignum] -- dead code). (2) Replace mpstrings dmaExec with bcopy of N64_MPSTRINGS_SIZE=320 bytes from confignum*320, into the head of the PC mpstrings struct (description[200] + aibotnames[0..7] = 320 bytes matches N64 layout exactly), with bzero of the whole PC struct first to leave aibotnames[8..31] zeroed. Bots 9..32 fall back to legacy g_BotConfigsArray naming. Build verify clean four-target via build-session.ps1 -Session b323: client 55.5 MB, updater 12.3 MB, server 22.4 MB, tests 24.6 MB. Audit append in context/audits/catalog-universality-pivot-plan-2026-05-02.md 'BYOR post-boot AV triaged' section. Bug ledger entry at B-323. Note: NOT a BYOR-completion issue -- this AV exists in BOTH pre-BYOR and post-BYOR builds; the user's prompt framing was inaccurate.
cards.notes: Worktree competent-saha-a202bb. SHA pending merge. B-323 in bugs.md.

cards.title: Dev Window Clear Worktrees button (replaces Prune)
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-11 (flamboyant-ride-cc996f). Mike's report: existing build-tool button doesn't actually clear worktrees. Diagnosis: BtnPruneWorktrees ran only `git worktree prune -v`, which clears stale registry entries (registry-pointing-at-deleted-dir) but never removes on-disk worktrees or their branches. With 18 worktrees on disk + 27 prunable registry entries at session start, a click cleared the 27 ghost entries and left the 18 active dirs untouched. Fix: full clear flow with disk-space accounting in devtools/dev-window-v2/dev-window-v2.ps1. Button label/content -> 'Clear Worktrees...'. On click: enumerate .claude/worktrees/ via async runspace (git worktree list --porcelain joined with on-disk Get-ChildItem), compute per-dir recursive size via DirectoryInfo.EnumerateFiles, skip reparse points to avoid junction loops. Modal WPF dialog (Show-WorktreeClearDialog) with DataGrid: checkbox + Name + Branch + Last Modified + Size, header showing on-disk count + total size + stale-prunable count, an 'Also prune N stale registry entries' checkbox (default ON when N>0), Select All / Select None / Cancel / Clear Selected buttons, live 'Selected: K worktrees, B' summary that updates on each cell edit. Skips the currently-active worktree. Worker scriptblock ($script:WorktreeClearWorker): for each selected entry, try `git worktree remove <path>`, fall back to `git worktree remove --force <path>` on dirty/untracked failure, then fall back to Remove-Item -Recurse -Force if the dir still exists. After removal, probe `git show-ref --verify --quiet refs/heads/<branch>` and run `git branch -D <branch>` if the branch still exists (worktree remove does not delete branches). Optional `git worktree prune -v` after the per-entry loop. Returns per-row report with size before, freed bytes, and step trace; UI logs each step in the Log tab and pops a Done dialog with totals. INPC row model (PD2V2.WorktreeEntry) added to the consolidated Add-Type block so DataGridCheckBoxColumn two-way binding works correctly with Select All / Select None refreshes. End-to-end verification on real worktree set: synthetic test worktree (1.04 GB on disk, branch test/wt-clear-test-*) created, enumerated, cleared via the same worker logic the GUI button drives -- worktree dir gone, branch deleted, prune ran exit 0. PowerShell bug fixed during verify: inside an `@(...)` array literal, `"refs/heads/" + $branch` was being parsed as TWO elements (string + unary-+ var) because comma binds tighter than +; parenthesised the concat to force binary-+ inside the element. Same bug would have existed in the GUI button's worker -- both call sites fixed. Scripts-only change; no C/C++ touched. .claude/scratch/ added to .gitignore. Test script at .claude/scratch/test-worktree-clear-e2e.ps1 (untracked, kept for future regression checks).

cards.title: Kanban server self-start + auto-exit on tab close
cards.description: SHIPPED 2026-05-11 (worktree peaceful-babbage-26b748). Kanban server now ephemeral: spawned by Dev Window v2 button (c117) and self-terminates when no tab is heartbeating. Page POSTs /heartbeat every 5s; on beforeunload sends navigator.sendBeacon('/shutdown-now', ...). Server tracks _last_heartbeat_at under a lock and runs a daemon watcher thread (2s interval) that calls server.shutdown() once idle exceeds KANBAN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S (default 15). Startup grace: _last_heartbeat_at = time.time() + STARTUP_GRACE_S (default 30) so a slow browser launch is not a problem. /shutdown-now is cooperative: backdates the clock to fire SHUTDOWN_NOW_GRACE_S (default 6) seconds later, but any heartbeat from another tab resets it so multi-tab close-one keeps the server alive. /shutdown-now is idempotent. Env vars KANBAN_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S, KANBAN_STARTUP_GRACE_S, KANBAN_SHUTDOWN_GRACE_S override defaults. Verified all 5 scenarios (cold-to-close, idle-no-beacon, multi-tab survives, launch-no-connect, manual launch smoke) via .claude/scratch/probe-ephemeral-kanban.py (gitignored). Dev Window v2 button itself unchanged: cold-start spawn + warm-start short-circuit both still correct because the existing server's heartbeat watcher just inherits the new tab's heartbeats.

cards.title: Commit message standard + commit-msg hook
cards.description: Structural commit message format anchored to kanban cards, enforced at write time by .githooks/commit-msg. cards.title: B-350: airborne side-entry through overhead collision blockers
cards.description: Track the 2026-05-19 physics-collision slice even though it was started and completed in one session. Mike's CI Training playtest showed c038/B-339 improved top/bottom jump collision, but the player could still jump sideways through overhead solid blockers and could get stuck above a doorway or inside a new blocker. Dynamic couch collision looked correct after moving the couch.
cards.notes:
Code/build slice completed 2026-05-19. Root cause: player airborne movement applied horizontal X/Z first, then bwalkUpdateVertical() only swept move=(0, verticalDelta, 0), so side-entry during a jump could bypass the side plane before vertical clamping. Fix: src/game/bondwalk.c adds bwalkClampAirborneSideEntry(), an upward diagonal capsuleSweep() from bondprevpos to the already-applied X/Z plus verticalDelta; on hit it rolls X/Z back to the safe fraction and clamps/kills upward velocity for ceiling-class hits. Test fixture now covers side-wall rendered triangles. Verification passed: scoped git diff --check, b350side tests target, focused [physics][jump] (99 assertions / 4 cases), and b350side all-target build. Manual CI Training retest remains the closure gate.
2026-05-22 B-367 follow-up: Mike reported the jumping player still clips into walls, ceilings, or corners. Root cause was the remaining horizontal half of the movement-order split: apex/descent lateral motion still committed through the legacy cylinder path before any capsule mesh repair ran. Fix: bwalkClampAirborneLateralEntry() now runs immediately after horizontal movement and before speed correction when airborne, uses the collision-owned capsule mesh sweep from bondprevpos, rolls X/Z back on wall/ceiling/corner hits, and ignores floor-class hits. Verification passed: focused [physics][jump] (105 assertions / 4 cases) and jump367 all-target build. Manual retest remains the closure gate.
Priority pass 2026-05-20: Collision critical path. Manual CI Training retest remains the gate before broader gameplay-stability work is treated as reliable.

cards.title: Updater stale cleanup should recycle user-visible removals
cards.description: Follow-up from Mike's question: when updater cleanup removes stale install-root files or folders, user-visible payload cleanup should send items to the Windows Recycle Bin instead of permanently deleting them.
cards.notes: Recommended policy: stale install payload paths use the Windows shell recycle/undo delete path; generated updater internals such as downloaded zips, sidecar version files, .old updater exe cleanup, and staging/temp files can remain permanent deletes. If recycle fails for a user-visible stale path, log it and leave the file in place rather than falling back to permanent deletion.

subtasks.notes: Use SHFileOperation or IFileOperation with undo/recycle semantics. Keep helper scoped to Windows updater cleanup paths.

subtasks.title: Use recycle-delete only for stale install payload cleanup
subtasks.notes: Apply to cleanupStaleFiles in both the in-client updater and standalone updater. Do not change permanent deletion for updater-generated temp artifacts.

subtasks.title: Log recycle success/failure and preserve on failure
subtasks.notes: If recycle deletion fails, record the failure in the relevant client/updater log and leave the file or folder in place.

cards.title: Modding external-format .pdmod archive pipeline
cards.description: Implement the modder-facing mod archive pipeline: typed .pd* files remain the content-unit format, their payloads become normal external files plus grouped INI/TSV metadata wherever practical, and .pdmod acts as the bundle/transport envelope for sharing and online-required content delivery.
cards.notes: Done 2026-05-20. Full-external-format boundary: typed *.pdxxx files are the preferred mod content units; their payloads are standard authored files plus grouped INI/TSV metadata; .pdmod is the bundle/transport envelope for sharing, Public Mods, and online-required delivery; authored .bin files are invalid in both content units and transport archives. Runtime-generated cache stays private, readable, rebuildable, and unshipped. All subtasks passed format validation, targeted/static compatibility checks, runtime smokes, context updates, and queued modpipe all build. Final closure added Public Mods install behavior: received .pdmod downloads validate, install into mods/installed, and refresh the mod registry.

cards.title: Asset Pipeline: clean self-contained archive layouts
cards.description: Define the clean self-contained format for every typed or otherwise referenceable asset family first, then rebuild extraction/examples/validators to match those frozen contracts. Human-authored files stay obvious at archive root or in purpose-named folders; machine/provenance/validation data moves under _meta/. Every archive remains fully self-contained: all descriptor, source-format, material, graph, nested-descriptor, and payload references must resolve inside the archive or inside an embedded typed archive. .pdmod remains transport only.
cards.notes: Created 2026-05-21 from Mike's request to walk each asset type and implement the clean-but-functional archive shape. Reprioritized 2026-05-22 as the top Asset Pipeline migration plan. Process order is locked: first define every asset-family format, starting with c3832 for .pdweapon; then freeze the contracts; then rebuild extraction/examples/validators in the full sweep. Shared contract: root descriptor required; no .pdwpn; no authored .bin; no reference-only dependency closure; duplicate embedded payloads are allowed on disk and deduped after ingestion by catalog identity and canonical SHA-256. Preferred archive zones are authoring files first, nested typed dependencies second, and _meta/ for manifest.json, inventory.json, provenance.json, validation reports, source handles, SHA rows, and compatibility bookkeeping. During transition, scanners/loaders may accept old root manifest.json and root SHA sidecars but new emitters should write _meta/ and release validation should fail stale installed outputs that are non-zip, .pdwpn, .bin-backed, descriptor-less, or unresolved internally. c3832 is the detailed .pdweapon format card and sits immediately under this migration plan. Approved 2026-05-23 first format decisions: .pdweapon, .pdprojectile, .pdentity, .pdmaterial, and .pdtexture are recorded on this single tracker. Higher-level assets link typed dependencies by catalog ID and self-contained exports embed those dependency assets as intact typed archives under dependencies/assets; they do not absorb dependency internals into the parent schema. Approved 2026-05-23 second format batch: .pdcharacter, .pdhead, .pdbody, .pdarena, and .pdscenario are recorded on this single tracker. Character is an assembler/meta asset; body owns skeleton and first-person hands; head owns head-specific rig/expression data; arena wraps playable multiplayer selection metadata around an embedded scenario; scenario owns level content and spawn profiles for default, gametype/team, CTF/objective, and mission-phase respawn cases. Approved 2026-05-23 third format batch: .pdmesh, .pdanim, .pdsfx, .pdvoice, and .pdsong are recorded on this single tracker. Mesh owns reusable geometry and rig-facing model data; animation owns reusable timelines/events/retargeting metadata; SFX owns atomic sound sources and playback metadata; voice owns spoken-line metadata, per-locale audio variants, subtitle bindings, voice-mod override compatibility, and global-language fallback behavior while .pdlang owns text strings; song owns editable sequence/track music data and adaptive playback metadata. Approved 2026-05-24 final format batch: .pdui, .pdfont, and .pdlang are recorded on this tracker, and all family formats are frozen in context/designs/modding/asset-archive-clean-formats.md. UI owns reusable texture/chrome assets with readable layout/nine-slice metadata; font owns vector or decoded bitmap font sources plus metrics/kerning; lang owns UTF-8 strings.tsv text banks while voice owns spoken audio. c3824-s1 shared two-zone validation/migration is done 2026-05-24: policy/scanner/loader/emitters/package gates now enforce the migration-vs-release boundary, with _meta/manifest.json and _meta/*.sha256 as new output. Next c3824 work is c3824-s20/c3824-s18, the broad extraction/examples/validators/release-gate sweep with deeper recursive internal reference closure. c3824-s18 examples/docs/package-gate slice is done 2026-05-24: recursive validation now checks descriptor, GLTF, OBJ/MTL, JSON, and embedded typed-archive references; typed-pdxxx-basic examples now cover every frozen family with _meta/manifest.json and mesh.ini. Remaining c3824 work is c3824-s20, the stale extraction/installed-output cleanup and release-gate sweep. c3824 is wrapped 2026-05-24: final release packaging gate validates the assembled dist tree before zip creation and fails stale typed outputs that are .pdwpn, non-zip, descriptor-less, legacy .pdmesh model.ini, root-metadata, or .bin-backed. No manual retest required for this headless validator/examples/release-gate card. Asset decision intake 2026-05-24 final: Mike approved all 35 Asset Decisions rows. New first-class families are .pdskin, .pdeffect, .pdprop, .pdvehicle, .pdmission, .pdgamemode, .pdbotprofile, .pdhud, and .pdtheme. .pdtool is deferred from the current asset implementation sweep but is a high-priority secure tool/plugin package follow-up. .pdentity remains behavior/archetype-focused and can depend on .pdprop for physical object payloads, including Laptop Gun-style deployed entities. .pdmaterial is classic-first but PBR-extensible; future PBR material payloads should remain standalone material assets. .pdscenario owns world/map content and maps to new ASSET_SCENARIO, separate from ASSET_ARENA, ASSET_MISSION, and ASSET_GAMEMODE. .pdmesh owns geometry, UVs, hierarchy, sockets, LODs, skinning, and collision proxy; textures/materials are typed dependencies with model_specific or reusable tags. Raw editable source files are allowed when owned by that family, while cross-family resources embed as intact typed archives under dependencies/assets. Mod utilities must export files in an easily accessible way for modders and import/reconstruct them as valid typed assets. Validators fail unresolved references unless the archive embeds the dependency or declares an approved base dependency with catalog id, compatibility/version/hash where available, reason, and on-disk/catalog provider source. Approved mapping decisions include ASSET_MATERIAL for .pdmaterial, ASSET_FONT for .pdfont, unified ASSET_AUDIO with strict category/channel/mod tags for .pdsfx/.pdvoice/.pdsong, and ASSET_MODEL reuse for .pdmesh. No authored .bin files belong in any asset archive. Post-decision load/use sweep 2026-05-24: context/designs/modding/asset-archive-clean-formats.md now includes all approved game-content families through .pdtheme, the .pdtool deferral note, and a per-family load/utilization closure matrix for the extraction implementation card c3838.

cards.title: Kanban: remote phone board and card sessions
cards.description: Add one-click Dev Window paths that start and stop the Kanban board for phone access from a different network, show/copy a join link, keep routing scoped to the Kanban localhost service only, and make the phone UI list-first with full-screen card editing plus card-scoped and ad-hoc Codex session controls.
cards.notes:
Remote mode uses KANBAN_REMOTE_TOKEN plus a localhost-only cloudflared tunnel to the chosen 127.0.0.1 Kanban port. It keeps normal local 7531 free, prefers remote port 7533, and falls forward if needed. Local Open Kanban verifies tokenless /api/state before reuse so it still works without Cloudflare or a token. Sessions can be opened full-screen from phone, render a clean response-only transcript, accept follow-up messages through codex exec resume, queue multiple prompts while a turn is running, steer a selected queued prompt to the front, answer plan-style choice questions with tap buttons, and can be started ad-hoc without a card. Remote mode does not enable WARP, set a system proxy, configure an exit node, or change Windows routes.

x_asset_archive_decisions.summary: Asset archive format freeze review recommendations before implementation.

items.recommendation: Keep as the weapon meta asset: weapon.ini, weapon-owned behavior and bindings, intact typed dependency archives under dependencies/assets, and _meta. .pdmod stays transport only.
items.decision_needed: Confirm this final clean layout, and confirm older sample shapes with root behavior.graph.json, hand.gltf, loose model, or loose audio should be migrated away.
items.recorded_label: Approved decision recorded on tracker card

items.recommendation: Keep as the projectile behavior asset: projectile.ini, flight, collision, damage, lifecycle, behavior data, typed visual/audio/effect/entity dependencies, and _meta.
items.decision_needed: Confirm projectiles are first-class catalog assets even when normally embedded by weapons.
items.recorded_label: Approved decision recorded on tracker card

items.recommendation: Keep as the graph-authored entity/archetype asset: entity.ini, bindings.json, optional behavior.graph.json, optional composition.json, typed dependencies, and _meta.
items.decision_needed: Confirm whether ordinary props remain separate .pdprop assets or are folded into .pdentity.
items.additional_info: .pdprop and .pdentity should both exist, but they should not mean the same thing. A .pdprop is the physical/world object: model, collision, materials, sockets, placement tags, and simple interaction hooks. A .pdentity is a behavior/archetype wrapper for something active: deployed, armed, AI-driven, scripted, or stateful. Laptop Gun fits this cleanly: the visible gun/turret object can be a .pdprop dependency, while .pdentity owns turret behavior, targeting, deploy state, animations, and links back to the owning weapon/player.
items.proposed_decision: Keep .pdentity behavior-focused and let it embed or depend on .pdprop when it needs a physical object. Simple crates, doors, scenery, pickups, or vehicles can be .pdprop/.pdvehicle without a .pdentity wrapper. Behavior-heavy deployables use .pdentity.
items.answer_prompt: Approve this split, or tell me you want .pdentity to be the broad meta asset for all world objects with .pdprop always underneath it.
items.recorded_label: Approved decision recorded on tracker card

items.recommendation: Keep as render and surface material data: material.ini, parameters, texture slot bindings, variants, compatibility tags, typed dependencies, and _meta.
items.decision_needed: Confirm .pdmaterial should get a first-class catalog type instead of mapping to ASSET_NONE.
items.additional_info: Yes, we can make the format PBR-ready without forcing PBR into the first implementation. material.ini can carry the classic/current render fields now, plus optional future slots such as workflow = classic or pbr, base_color, normal, metallic, roughness, occlusion, emissive, opacity, and clearcoat maps.
items.proposed_decision: Reserve optional PBR fields and compatibility tags now. Current runtime can ignore, approximate, or validate them until the renderer supports them fully.
items.recorded_label: Approved decision recorded on tracker card

items.recommendation: Keep as editable image source: texture.ini, source image data, alpha, palette, mip and import settings, usage tags, and _meta.
items.decision_needed: Confirm no authored runtime .bin payload is allowed in texture archives.
items.recorded_label: Approved decision recorded on tracker card

items.title: .pdentity
items.prompt: Confirm whether ordinary props remain separate .pdprop assets or are folded into .pdentity.
items.recommendation:
Keep as the graph-authored entity/archetype asset: entity.ini, bindings.json, optional behavior.graph.json, optional composition.json, typed dependencies, and _meta.

Additional info: .pdprop and .pdentity should both exist, but they should not mean the same thing. A .pdprop is the physical/world object: model, collision, materials, sockets, placement tags, and simple interaction hooks. A .pdentity is a behavior/archetype wrapper for something active: deployed, armed, AI-driven, scripted, or stateful. Laptop Gun fits this cleanly: the visible gun/turret object can be a .pdprop dependency, while .pdentity owns turret behavior, targeting, deploy state, animations, and links back to the owning weapon/player.

Recommendation: Keep .pdentity behavior-focused and let it embed or depend on .pdprop when it needs a physical object. Simple crates, doors, scenery, pickups, or vehicles can be .pdprop/.pdvehicle without a .pdentity wrapper. Behavior-heavy deployables use .pdentity.

Separate map/scenario content from multiplayer rules. .pdgamemode owns rules; .pdscenario owns map content.

Additional info: This is the runtime enum half of the .pdscenario decision. ASSET_MAP is simple, but slightly vague. ASSET_SCENARIO is clearer because the archive stores more than geometry: setup, pads, collision, visual data, spawn profiles, and dependencies.

Recommendation: Add ASSET_SCENARIO and map .pdscenario to it. Keep ASSET_ARENA for multiplayer wrappers, ASSET_MISSION for campaign wrappers, and ASSET_GAMEMODE for rules.

items.title: Raw sidecars in clean archives
items.prompt: Confirm release-format .pdhead, .pdbody, .pdmesh, .pdarena, and .pdweapon samples should migrate away from loose cross-family sidecars.
items.recommendation:
Allow raw editable source files only when they are owned by that family. Cross-family resources should be intact embedded typed archives under dependencies/assets.

Additional info: Raw editable source files are fine when they are owned by that archive family. Examples: .pdtexture owns image sources; .pdmesh owns mesh source geometry; .pdsfx owns WAV/source audio; .pdscenario owns map OBJ/TSV/setup source. But cross-family resources should not be loose sidecars inside another family.

Recommendation: Release-format archives embed cross-family resources as intact typed archives under dependencies/assets. Example: .pdhead embeds mesh.pdmesh and material/texture dependencies, not loose GLTF/PNG files. .pdweapon embeds .pdmesh/.pdsfx/.pdprojectile/.pdentity dependencies, not loose model/audio files at root.

Answer needed: Approve this raw-owned-files versus typed-dependency rule?

items.title: Catalog references inside examples
items.prompt: Confirm validators should reject unresolved example-local dependency refs unless the ref is declared as a base-game dependency.
items.recommendation:
Example archives with bindings to body/head/rig/texture/material/localization assets must embed those dependencies or use an explicit approved base dependency.

Additional info: Self-contained exports should not be reference-only shells. If an archive points at another authored asset, that dependency must be embedded unless it is deliberately using a base-game dependency that resolves through catalog/on-disk provider source. Base dependency records need to be explicit so validators know the missing dependency is intentional, not broken.

Recommendation: Validators should fail unresolved references unless the archive either embeds the dependency as a typed archive or declares an approved base dependency with catalog id, compatibility/version/hash where available, reason, and on-disk/catalog provider source.
